content: If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favorable.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

In Seneca's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
